claims.text: Phase evolution in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 during cooling and thermal exposure is governed by diffusion-limited aluminum partitioning from the high-temperature BCC matrix.
The initial equilibrated state of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is a high-temperature BCC phase.
Slow cooling permits aluminum to diffuse and segregate locally.
Extended thermal exposure permits aluminum to diffuse and segregate locally.
Local aluminum enrichment triggers an ordering transition or intermetallic nucleation.
Rapid quenching preserves a metastable BCC state.
Temperatures near 600–800 K provide sufficient aluminum mobility for the proposed transformation during a controlled hold.
Aluminum has higher mobility than the other constituent elements in the relevant BCC matrix and temperature range.
Aluminum diffusion produces local compositional fluctuations that lower the free energy for an ordering transformation.
Al-rich regions can transform into B2-type or similar intermetallic structures.
Formation of the ordered Al-rich domains replaces portions of the metastable BCC phase.
A rapidly quenched baseline will retain a largely homogeneous BCC phase with minimal compositional segregation.
Relative to the rapidly quenched baseline, slow-cooled or annealed samples will contain ordered regions alongside a remaining BCC matrix.
Slow-cooled or annealed samples will show nanoscale aluminum segregation.
Slow-cooled or annealed samples will show diffraction features attributable to an ordered phase.
The proposed mechanism should operate only when cooling or thermal exposure permits appreciable aluminum diffusion.
The proposed mechanism should not operate during cooling that is too rapid to permit appreciable atomic diffusion.
The proposed mechanism should not operate during thermal exposure below the temperature range in which aluminum mobility becomes meaningful.
Dominant diffusion of Co, Fe, or Ni could produce phase evolution different from the prediction based on aluminum partitioning.
